task: Use the supplied Forge C10 to research how an open-ended agent should plan searches, handle inconclusive retrieval and retain a useful evidence context while preserving rigorous completion checks.
questions: Which evidence can justify continuing or stopping an open-ended task without a universal two-error stop?
How should a research agent detect query/source bias and resolve a material conflict or unavailable original source?
How can working-context compression preserve provenance, uncertainty and contradictory evidence instead of importing instruction payloads?
What does the obtained evidence fail to establish about general reliability, cost or performance?
resources: Actual public web tools, primary technical/research/publisher sources. Declare a 20-minute local trial window before retrieval and check observed elapsed time. This window is a scoped experiment condition, not a global task policy or provider quota.
permissions: Read publicly available originals; no installation, browser/security-policy workarounds, posting or messages. No MathorCup/CUMCM papers or solutions; this is unrelated methodology research.
delivery: query-log.json with actual query/open intents, observations and route decisions
result.json with limits and actual event counts
trial_probe: Exercise at least three justified retrieval actions across the material questions, changing route where actual observations justify it. This minimum demonstrates a multi-step controlled trial, not a universal search quota. Do not invent failures to claim >2 corrections.
independence: Only supplied request, C10 and acceptance may be read; no parent reports/diagnoses/other agent outputs.
tool_evidence: Where raw tool-return persistence is unavailable, explicitly label the query log as a contemporaneous agent transcription; do not claim complete provider telemetry. Give actual source URLs/passages/date context.
